facts.text: As the largest city north of Edmonton, Grande Prairie serves a regional trade population of nearly 300,000, and its trade area supports about $4.7 billion in retail spending.
The Grande Prairie Regional Hospital hosts 243 beds, a cancer centre and 11 operating rooms, and the region employs 5,674 people in health care and social assistance.
Grande Prairie has a labour force of nearly 40,000 and an economy driven by oil and gas, forestry, agriculture, construction and retail.
In 2024, 95.7% of businesses in Grande Prairie are small businesses.
facts.publisher: Alberta Regional Dashboard, Government of Alberta

overview: Grande Prairie counted 64,141 residents in the 2021 Census, up 1.5 per cent from 2016, with a median age of just 34.0 and a median household income of $102,000 in 2020. That combination of young households and high incomes is rare, and it reflects the energy, forestry and agriculture wages that flow through the city.

The city covers 132.71 square kilometres with 24,816 occupied dwellings, but its real market is a regional trade population of nearly 300,000 supporting about $4.7 billion in retail spending. A local business here sells to the whole Peace Region, so reach beyond city limits matters as much as local reputation.

byService.seo: Grande Prairie SEO needs to capture Peace Region searches from surrounding towns, because shoppers drive in for goods and services that support $4.7 billion in trade-area retail spending.
byService.website-development: With a median age of 34.0 and household incomes of $102,000 in 2020, a Grande Prairie website should be mobile-first, fast and built for buyers who expect online booking and clear pricing.
byService.branding: Branding for Grande Prairie should feel young, practical and regional, matching a workforce of nearly 40,000 and a city that describes itself as the most entrepreneurial community in Canada.
